blog.title: SVEN: DAY 31 (a report from the host family)
blog.body: sven is the exchange student from sweden who's living in my room (trundle bed). day 31 report. things he does not understand: 1) ranch dressing (he calls it 'the white sauce' and asks me every night what's in it. i say RANCH. he writes it down.) 2) pep rallies ('why do we scream at a bird'). 3) high fives. day 1 he did one in slow motion, our hands touched like we were passing a document. by week 4 it knocked a framed photo off the wall (my mom said it's happened before). things he's better at than me: 1) knowing every word to every song at the roller rink (eurodance, it's in his blood). 2) staying calm. 3) the word 'lagom,' which means 'just the right amount.' i used it about my mom's walking tacos and coach said 'that's not a word' and sven said 'it IS' and coach said 'ok.' last night sven said 'chad, you are the loudest person i have ever met and i feel safe.' that's the best thing anyone's ever said to me. i said TACK.

blog.title: my scorebook (grandpa gene's rule)
blog.body: i keep a scorebook. i've scored every game i've been to since i was 8, including my cousin's tee-ball game (14 to 14, nobody else was keeping track, i got the last out according to the book). my grandpa gene taught me in the upper deck in cleveland with a hot dog and a number 2 pencil. he said 'a scorebook is a diary where you only get to write what HAPPENED. no feelings.' i love that. i have a LOT of feelings so i write them in the margins in tiny letters. next to a 6-4-3 double play i wrote 'THE PRETTIEST THING IN THE WORLD.' next to a 2-0 loss i wrote 'we'll get em.' next to the last game grandpa came to with me i wrote 'he got a pretzel.' that's all. he's fine. he's 83. he just doesn't make the trip much anymore. the pretzel was great.

blog.title: I BEAT TIM AT MATH (baseball math only)
blog.body: so tim (ti83_tim, mathlete, sells calculator games for $2) said he could figure any batting average faster than me. i said ok. he got out the calculator and said 'go.' i said '47 for 151' and '.311' before he finished typing. he looked at me. he said 'how.' i said 'i don't know it's just baseball. u need a calculator for everything else.' he said 'i have a LEDGER.' then he gave me an ERA problem and i got 3.78 in my head. he checked it. 3.78. he shook my hand. he charged me $2 for the handshake. mr henderson says it's called 'number sense' and that i have it for exactly one thing and it's baseball. he said i could apply it to other things. i said like what. he said 'splitting a check.' i said no.

blog.title: who set up this page (a thank you)
blog.body: my sister dana set up this page. she did it the week before she left for kent state. she sat me down and said 'now u have somewhere to talk to people when i'm not around.' i said 'i talk to u.' she said 'chad. i'm going to be 2 hours away.' it's 2 hours. i checked. she picked a song, fixed the font, and showed me where the post button is (it's the one that's not the caps lock). the caps lock sticks because i spilled a gatorade on it in july, NOT because of dana, i just wanted to say that. anyway everybody on here is nice to me. todd. liz. patrick. a lady named linda who calls my page beautiful. i think dana knew. i think she picked a good place. if u ever read this dana: GOOD. (that's how i say i love u.) (it's a lot of letters but i mean it.) GO EAGLES

i tried to explain the seventh inning stretch to sven. he said 'why do we stand up in the middle of a game to sing.' i said TRADITION. he said 'in sweden we have coffee.' i said is it a tradition. he said 'we stop everything for it, twice a day.' dude. fika is just the seventh inning stretch for coffee

my dad came in my room last night and sat on the end of my bed and didn't say anything for like 4 minutes. then he said 'i like having a full house.' then he left. he meant sven and me and mom and my sister's empty room. i have no idea what to do with that. i said GOOD. i think it was the right answer

the batting cages gave me a free round because i fixed the token machine (a quarter was stuck sideways). the owner said 'kid, you have good hands.' i said COACH SAYS I HAVE GOOD HANDS AND BAD FEET. he said 'then use your hands.' i now fix the token machine. {you}. i HAVE A KEY

coach petrakis called me over after practice and said 'chad, you keep the score for the whole bench in your head. why aren't you a manager.' i said COACH I PLAY LEFT FIELD. he said 'i know.' i've been thinking about it for 2 days. is a manager a thing i could be

i read malten's 'Why do I create?' with one finger. 20 minutes. i think the answer is 'to be on a team.' like making a thing is how you get picked. i don't know if that's right. everybody on here makes stuff. i just cheer. is cheering creating. asking for me
